Cascades métalliques de vaisselles versées à la vapeur sur les tables… éparpillement de cuillers… bouteilles attrapées au vol… soupières de corps de garde tenant en leurs flancs rebondis des mares écumantes où plongent les louches avec le plouf sonore des grenouilles en alerte…

La Seine n’avait pas bougé depuis ce soir-là. D’ailleurs elle n’avait pas bougé depuis le « plouf » de Buridan clos dans son sac, amours mortes, et coulait toujours, autres amours mortes, sous le pont Mirabeau.

examples.text: He heard the plops of rain on the roof.

examples.text: Stooping, she picked up another pebble, sounded out the word again, and tossed it into the shallow water near the path, where it plopped into the water, sending out circles from where it fell.

glosses: To land heavily or loosely.

examples.text: He plopped down on the sofa to watch TV.

glosses: To hit or expel liquid at.

examples.text: The children were splashing each other playfully in the sea.
When she comes in the door, splash her with perfume.

glosses: To create an impact or impression; to print, post, or publicize prominently.

examples.text: The headline was splashed across newspapers everywhere.

The March 5, 1978 issue of National Reader […] contained an exciting front page headline -- "Most Major Hollywood Stars Are Gay or Bisexual!!!!" Splashed on the cover are photos of Rock Hudson, Shaun and David Cassidy, […] and, last but not least, Lily Tomlin.
Now it's big black cars and Riviera views / And your lover in the foyer doesn't even know you / And your secrets end up splashed on the news front page

glosses: To spend (money).

examples.text: After pay day I can afford to splash some cash and buy myself a motorbike.

glosses: To roughly fill with color.

examples.text: This was pure theatre, with a 60,000 crowd at Wembley adding colour to the fight to face either England or Denmark in Sunday's final, the stadium splashed with the red of Spain at one end and the victorious blue of Italy at the other as crowds flocked back in ever bigger numbers after pandemic restrictions were lifted.

glosses: To launch a ship.

examples.text: In the two years following Midway, Japanese shipyards managed to splash only six additional fleet carriers. The United States in the same period added seventeen, along with ten medium carriers and eighty-six escort carriers.

glosses: To shoot down (an aircraft) over water.

examples.text: Planes were sighted at about 5000 yards, fire was opened at 4500 yards; the first plane was splashed about 1800 yards from the ship, the second was splashed about 3000 yards from the ship and rudder shifted to hard right.

glosses: To stab (a person), causing them to bleed.

Grab him, don't panic, rambo under my jacket
Nap him, splash him, then I'm petrol bath my jacket
